question: How many of the 90 frozen benchmark items carry an anchor that resolves to a corpus provision?

corpus.other_framework_packs: NONE — no GDPR, CRA, DORA, NIS2 or CSRD pack or snapshot exists

finding: 14% of items anchor to a corpus provision. 84% carry a prose anchor with no article reference at all. FIVE of six axes have ZERO corpus linkage — safety, provenance, conformance, openness and continuity are anchored entirely to hand-written prose.
why_five_axes_are_zero: Those axes are not about EU AI Act articles. DefBench items anchor to harm categories, PQCBench to cryptographic properties, OSSBench to licence terms. Their prose anchors are not sloppy — they are anchored to a DIFFERENT corpus that does not exist. There is no PQC standards pack, no licence-text pack, no C2PA spec pack.
correction_to_the_plan: The retrofit proposal assumed 417 provisions across six frameworks (126 AI Act + 99 GDPR + 71 CRA + 64 DORA + 46 NIS2 + 11 CSRD) and therefore a '224-provision measurement gap'. Measured: ONE pack exists (eu-ai-act@1.0.0, 21 provisions) and no snapshot directory for any other framework. The gap map cannot be computed from a corpus that is not there. The AI Act term alone is 21, not 126.
what_is_actually_actionable: Retrofit the 13 governance items that DO cite a corpus article to carry provision_hash instead of prose. Smallest change, proves the chain end to end, immediately auditable.
The 10 governance items with no article reference are candidates for adjudication against the 21 provisions — generate, adjudicate, admit only what survives.
The 1 item citing Art 2 is a genuine gap: Art 2 (scope) is not in the 21-provision snapshot. Either extend the snapshot or reclassify the item.

For the other five axes, a provision_hash retrofit is not possible until a corpus for their domain exists. Recording them as prose-anchored is honest; pretending otherwise would make them LOOK rigorous while being unverifiable — the exact failure mode the plan warns about.
the_plan_is_right_about_this: 'A corpus-derived item with a wrong label is worse than no item, because the hash makes it look rigorous.' That is exactly correct, and it is why the 76 prose-anchored items must NOT be given hashes they do not have.
